title: 16-Layer ThSi2/YbF3 Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack with Log-Normal Seeding
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack using ThSi2 (high-index) and YbF3 (low-index) on CaF2 substrate will achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm through constructive interference, while providing stopband rejection at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm through destructive interference, with 16 layers sufficient to reach >70% peak transmittance in passbands.
design_principle: Alternating quarter-wave layers at center wavelength 4.45 μm create a broad high-transmission region. The high index contrast (ThSi2 n≈3.0, YbF3 n≈1.5 in mid-IR) provides strong reflectivity in stopbands with fewer layers than lower-contrast pairs.
proposed_topology: Air | [ThSi2/YbF3]_8 | CaF2 substrate (16 finite layers total, 8 pairs)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: minimum layer thickness 6.0 nm to ensure film continuity
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating high/low index layers at λ/4 optical thickness create high reflectivity bands
Mid-IR material selection: ThSi2 and YbF3 have low absorption in 3-5 μm range per literature on IR filter design
expected_advantages: High index contrast reduces required layer count
16 layers leaves margin for future complexity
Log-normal seeding avoids local minima from deterministic quarter-wave start
known_risks: Material registry may not have ThSi2 or YbF3 optical constants
Quarter-wave stack produces single broad passband, may not separate CO/CO2 bands cleanly
16 layers may be insufficient for deep stopband rejection
execution_request_english: Design a 16-layer periodic dielectric stack on CaF2 substrate for mid-IR dual-band pass filter. Stack topology: Air | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | CaF2. Initialize all layer thicknesses using log-normal distribution centered at quarter-wave optical thickness for 4.45 μm (ThSi2 ~370 nm, YbF3 ~740 nm assuming n_H=3.0, n_L=1.5) with σ=0.15. Enforce hard minimum thickness 6.0 nm per layer and maximum 800 nm per layer. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm. Angle: 0 degrees (normal incidence). Polarization: unpolarized. Optimize 16 thickness variables to maximize mean transmittance in passbands (4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm) and minimize mean transmittance in stopbands (3600-4000 nm, 4850-5200 nm). Use coherent TMM with smatrix. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Previous route_03 iterations failed due to material_data (Ge/ZnS, Si3N4/MgF2 not in registry) and compilation error (NoneType in float conversion). This revision switches to ThSi2/YbF3 material pair with confirmed mid-IR applicability per evidence, enforces 6.0 nm minimum thickness to prevent validator collapse, uses log-normal initialization to avoid deterministic seeding issues, and ensures all numeric parameters are explicit floats to fix compilation.
